§95, p. 128: the causeway from the Granite Temple "straight up to the entrance of the temple of that Pyramid" is "a grand work, about 15 feet wide and over quarter of a mile long". Petrie writes "about", so the sigma is a foot and a half.

§95, p. 128: "over quarter of a mile long", a quarter of a mile being 1320 ft. A lower bound and not a length, so nothing is built from it; the causeway drawn between the two temples is checked against it.

How far the basalt platform is drawn proud of the ground. Petrie says in §28 that the pavement is "within two inches of the same level as" the limestone pavement round the Pyramid, and gives no thickness for the basalt; half a metre is chosen so the platform reads as the floor of a destroyed temple rather than vanishing into the ground it is flush with.

How deep the causeway is drawn. Petrie describes the rock "uniformly cut down to a sloping bed, on which has been laid apparently two layers of fine white limestone", all since torn up, and gives no depth; a metre draws the bed as a raised way along its ridge.
§96, p. 129 (Birdsall transcription): "The pillars in this hall are all monoliths of dark red granite, like that of the walls; they are 41 inches (2 cubits) square". 41 in.
§96, p. 129 (Birdsall transcription): the pillars are "174.2 high, weighing, therefore, about 13 tons each". 174.2 in.
§96, p. 129 (Birdsall transcription): "The two larger pillars, placed at the junction of the two parts of the hall, to support three beams each, are 58 inches wide". 58 in.
§96, p. 129 (Birdsall transcription): the beams are "41 inches square in the double colonnade". 41 in.
§96, p. 129 (Birdsall transcription): the beams are "47.8 to 48.4 deep in the single colonnade, where their span is greater"; the mean. 48.1 in.

§96, p. 129 (Birdsall transcription): "The shorter spans are 128, and the longer 145 inches"; the shorter are the double colonnade's. On Pl. vi the clear gaps there are 86 to 91 in between pillars of about 41, so the spans are centre to centre. 128 in.
§96, p. 129 (Birdsall transcription): the longer spans, the single colonnade's (clear gaps of 101.6 to 105.4 on Pl. vi between pillars of about 41: centre to centre). 145 in.
§96, p. 130: "Besides this great hall, with the colonnades 222.4 inches high". Pillar and single-colonnade beam: 174.2 + 48.1 = 222.3. 222.4 in.

§96, p. 131: the ventilators "were formed by sloping slits along the top edge of the walls, a few inches wide, and usually 41 inches long"; they "exist all along the Western part of the great hall". 41 in.
